facts.claim: Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) s35(2), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): 'Subject to this section, the author of a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work is the owner of any copyright subsisting in the work by virtue of this Part.'

Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) s35(3), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): 'The operation of any of the next three succeeding subsections in relation to copyright in a particular work may be excluded or modified by agreement.' (This covers s35(4) to (6), including the commissioned-photograph rule in s35(5).)

Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) s35(5), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): where 'a person makes, for valuable consideration, an agreement with another person for the taking of a photograph for a private or domestic purpose' (or the painting or drawing of a portrait or making of an engraving) and 'the work is made in pursuance of the agreement', 'the first-mentioned person is the owner of any copyright subsisting in the work by virtue of this Part'.

Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) s35(5), continued (AustLII, read 19 November 2026): 'but, if at the time the agreement was made that person made known, expressly or by implication, to the author of the work the purpose for which the work was required, the author is entitled to restrain the doing, otherwise than for that purpose, of any act comprised in the copyright in the work.'
Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) s35(7), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): '"private or domestic purpose" includes a portrait of family members, a wedding party or children.'

insider_details.detail: Under Australian law a wedding is named as a private or domestic purpose, and the default rule gives copyright in commissioned photos to the person who paid for them, but the Act lets the contract change that. Read the usage and copyright clause before you sign, and ask for what you need (print, share, album, publication) in writing.

Even where the couple owns the copyright, the photographer can restrain use beyond the purpose made known when the agreement was made, so if you might want images for something beyond the wedding itself, say so at booking and have it written into the agreement.
